claims.claim: FBAR is due April 15 with an automatic extension to October 15 that does not need to be requested
claims.raw_snippet: The FBAR is due April 15. Those who don't meet the April 15 due date must file by October 15, the automatically extended due date for the FBAR. They don't need to request the extension.

claims.claim: Form 8938 thresholds for specified individuals living outside the US are more than USD 200,000 last day or 300,000 any time if unmarried, and more than USD 400,000 last day or 600,000 any time if married filing jointly (בעברית: טופס 8938)
claims.raw_snippet: Specified individuals living outside the US: Unmarried individual (or married filing separately): Total value of assets was more than $200,000 on the last day of the tax year, or more than $300,000 at any time during the year. Married individual filing jointly: Total value of assets was more than $400,000 on the last day of the tax year, or more than $600,000 at any time during the year.

claims.claim: Form 8938 thresholds for specified individuals living in the US are more than USD 50,000 last day or 75,000 any time if unmarried, and more than USD 100,000 last day or 150,000 any time if married filing jointly
claims.raw_snippet: Married individual filing jointly: Total value of assets was more than $100,000 on the last day of the tax year, or more than $150,000 at any time during the year. Specified individuals living outside the US: Unmarried individual (or married filing separately): Total value of assets was more than $200,000 on the last day of the tax year, or more than $300,000 at any time during the year.

claims.claim: The willful FBAR penalty is the greater of the inflation adjusted 100,000 amount or 50 percent of the account balance at the violation date
claims.raw_snippet: For violations occurring after October 22, 2004, a penalty for each willful FBAR violation may be imposed up to the greater of the $100,000 penalty amount under 31 USC 5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I) , adjusted for inflation as described in paragraph (4), or 50% of the amount in the account at the time of the violation

claims.claim: A US citizen residing overseas gets an automatic 2 month extension to June 15 without requesting it
claims.raw_snippet: you are allowed an automatic 2-month extension to file your return without requesting an extension. If you use a calendar year, the regular due date of your return is April 15, and the automatic extended due date would be June 15.

claims.claim: A further extension to October 15 requires Form 4868 filed before the automatic 2 month extension date, and interest still accrues on tax unpaid at the regular due date (בעברית: טופס 4868)
claims.raw_snippet: you can request an additional extension to October 15 by filing Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time To File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return , before the automatic 2-month extension date. Even if you are allowed an extension, you will have to pay interest on any tax not paid by the regular due date of your return.

claims.claim: The streamlined foreign offshore non-residency requirement is no US abode and physical presence outside the US for at least 330 full days in one or more of the most recent 3 years for which the due date has passed
claims.raw_snippet: the individual did not have a U.S. abode and the individual was physically outside the United States for at least 330 full days.

claims.claim: Streamlined foreign offshore requires 3 years of delinquent or amended returns and 6 years of delinquent FBARs, with full tax and interest remitted
claims.raw_snippet: file delinquent or amended tax returns, together with all required information returns (e.g., Forms 3520, 5471, and 8938) and (2) for each of the most recent 6 years for which the FBAR due date has passed, file any delinquent FBARs (FinCEN Form 114, previously Form TD F 90-22.1). The full amount of the tax and interest due in connection with these filings must be remitted

claims.claim: An eligible streamlined foreign offshore filer is not subject to failure to file, failure to pay, accuracy related, information return, or FBAR penalties
claims.raw_snippet: A taxpayer who is eligible to use these Streamlined Foreign Offshore Procedures and who complies with all of the instructions outlined below will not be subject to failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalties, accuracy-related penalties, information return penalties, or FBAR penalties.

claims.claim: A foreign tax credit cannot be claimed for taxes on income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion, and taking the credit may be treated as revoking the election
claims.raw_snippet: If you elect to exclude either foreign earned income or foreign housing costs , you cannot take a foreign tax credit for taxes on income you exclude. If you do take the credit, one or both of the elections may be considered revoked.

claims.claim: A revoked foreign earned income exclusion choice cannot be re-made within 5 years without IRS approval, and claiming the foreign tax credit, additional child tax credit or earned income credit in a later year is treated as revoking the prior choice
claims.raw_snippet: if you decide to take the foreign tax credit, additional child tax credit, or earned income credit in a subsequent year, you will be considered to have revoked your prior choice. Note: You do not need to revoke a prior choice just because you have no foreign earned income or foreign housing costs for the year. If you revoked a choice and within 5 years again wish to choose the same exclusion, you must apply for IRS approval.

claims.claim: Late-payment penalties run from the extended due date for those qualifying for the 2 month extension; interest from April 15

Penalties for paying the tax late are assessed from the original due date of your return, unless you qualify for the automatic 2-month extension. In that situation, penalties for paying late are assessed from the extended due date

claims.raw_snippet: The IRS is required to notify the State Department of taxpayers certified as owing a seriously delinquent tax debt. Individuals and domestic entities must check the requirements and relevant reporting thresholds of each form and determine if they should file Form 8938 or FinCEN Form 114, or both

claims.raw_snippet: Affected taxpayers have until September 30, 2026 to file tax returns, make tax payments, and perform certain time-sensitive acts

claims.claim: Affected taxpayers include individuals whose principal residence is in Israel, the West Bank or Gaza, and those whose preparer or necessary records are located there
claims.raw_snippet: Any individual whose principal residence, and any business entity or sole proprietor whose principal place of business, is located in the State of Israel, the West Bank or Gaza (covered area); - Any individual affiliated with a recognized government or philanthropic organization and who is assisting in the covered area, such as a relief worker; - Any individual, business entity or sole proprietor, or estate or trust whose tax return preparer or records necessary to meet a deadline for postponed acts are located in the covered area

claims.claim: IRS applies relief automatically by prior-return address; affected taxpayers outside the covered area call the disaster hotline
claims.raw_snippet: The IRS automatically identifies taxpayers whose principal residence or principal place of business is located in the covered area based on previously filed returns and applies relief. Affected taxpayers whose principal residence or principal place of business is not located in the covered area should call the IRS disaster hotline

claims.claim: The postponed acts listed are filing and paying income, estate, gift, GST, excise and employment taxes, among others
claims.raw_snippet: These acts include, but are not limited to: - Filing any return of income tax, estate tax, gift tax, generation-skipping transfer tax, excise tax (other than firearms tax), harbor maintenance tax, or employment tax; - Paying any income tax, estate tax, gift tax, generation-skipping transfer tax, excise tax (other than firearms tax), harbor maintenance tax, or employment tax, or any installment of those taxes; - Making contributions to a qualified retirement plan; - Filing a petition with the Tax Court; - Filing a claim for credit or refund of any tax; and - Bringing suit upon a claim for credit or refund of any tax. This is not an exhaustive list.
